title: Integration & Surface Maturity Review (periodical run, fifth): trend vs the 2026-10-21 run. Is R7 in a fifth cycle after the workspace-api split, and what do the area-notes, per-request usage, model-routing and rebuilt periodical lanes add?
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="integration-surface-maturity" -->

**Periodical run: Integration & Surface Maturity, fifth run.** Origin **LIN-1336** (`generateIntegrationSurfaceMaturityPrompt()` in `lib/periodicals.js`; registry entry `id: 'integration-surface-maturity'`, `mode: 'advisory'`, `scope: 'repo'`). Prior runs: LIN-2383 (run 2), LIN-3105 (run 3), LIN-3765 (run 4). This is an **advisory, review-only** run. It produces one trend-framed maturity report for a human. It mints **no** follow-up tasks and writes **no** area-note entries.

This review is a **portfolio/meta layer over the other periodicals**. It is not one more sibling that re-inspects everything from scratch. Most of its evidence should come from what the sibling reviews, the area notes, prior audits and related tickets already found. Its own first-party inspection covers only what nothing else owns: FLOW surfaces, core/happy-path completeness, configuration, and the portfolio/META scorecard. Like the Stability Review and Recent Headwinds, it hands a human a maturity read across the whole system. It does not mint fix-work into territory another review already governs.

**Re-ground before you start.** Everything under *Orientation* was gathered on **2026-11-10** at **LinearViewer** `f5b1f5efa` and **simple-dispatcher** `5d8489e`. Treat it as pointers, not findings. Run `git fetch` in both repos, re-confirm every concrete claim at HEAD, and record any drift as your first finding, not as a reason to stop. Runs 3 and 4 each had second-reads catch claims that were stale or misfiled: a large modified subsystem filed as "unchanged" (run 3), and the whole consumer change set left un-inventoried (run 4). Hold yourself to that standard.

---

## 1. Read prior runs first: this review tracks trends

The series lives in `LinearViewer/docs/reviews/integration-surface-maturity-review-*.md`:

* `…-2026-07-17.md` is the **baseline**. Run 2 is `…-2026-08-29.md` and run 3 is `…-2026-09-26.md`.
* `…-2026-10-21.md` is **run 4** (LIN-3765/3766/3767/3768, PR #2036, squash `38760071`, merged 2026-10-23, scored at LinearViewer `c5694b68` / simple-dispatcher `bb1da78`). **Your delta is against run 4.** Its bulky evidence is in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-10-21/integration-surface-maturity/`.

Read run 4 in full. That includes its Trend Ledger (**51 scored ids: 21 MOD / 10 API / 20 FLOW, plus 1 META**), its *Ranked recommendations* table (R1–R17; R4, R5 and R10 resolved), its N/A justifications, its *Self-Audit*, its *Completeness %* note (≈88.6%, 180.75 of 204) and its *Adversarial Second-Read*.

Frame **every** surface and recommendation as a delta against run 4: new, unchanged, improved, worsened, resolved or retired. Never present a point-in-time snapshot. Surface maturity is a trajectory, and one snapshot cannot tell steady improvement from stagnation or regression. If you cannot find run 4, say so plainly and write this run as a new baseline. Do not invent a delta.

**Convention (confirm it still holds before relying on it).** Each run lands as `docs/reviews/integration-surface-maturity-review-YYYY-MM-DD.md` through a docs-only PR to `LinearViewer` `main`, from a branch such as `feat/lin-<this task>-integration-surface-maturity-review-5`. Bulky evidence goes in a dated folder under `docs/reviews/`. Run 4 hit a collision (`_evidence-2026-10-21/` already held 845 Design & Interface files), so check first and use your own subfolder or suffix, e.g. `_evidence-YYYY-MM-DD-isml/`. `ci-success` must be green (LinearViewer `CLAUDE.md`). If discovery genuinely finds no such place, put the full report in a comment on this task instead. Do not invent a new location.

## 2. Audit the scope before executing (widen, don't shrink)

Treat the scope below as a **starting point to extend, not a checklist to stay inside.** Before scoring, look for surfaces that are *in-remit but unlisted*: ones this review should cover that this description did not name. Fold them in. A scope you can only shrink is suspect. The expected move is to widen it to what the remit actually reaches.

Stay **broad in discovery and bounded in output.** A wider scope changes *what you examine*, never *what you report*. The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked, and a clean or near-empty result is a genuine outcome. This review mints no follow-up work at all, so breadth belongs in the search, not in padded output.

Run the sweep **by behaviour, not by name.** All five passes are required. Run 4's second-read showed that a Harbour-only added-file sweep misses whole lanes.

1. **Added files, both repos.** Enumerate every file added since run 4's pin: under `lib/`, `routes/` **and** `public/` in LinearViewer, and every non-test production module in simple-dispatcher. Resolve each one's production importers (ESM `from '…/<name>.js'`). Give each an explicit, cited disposition: new surface, folded into an existing id, or excluded with a reason. None may be silent, and the dispositions must sum to the file count.
2. **Deleted files.** Every deleted file that a run-4 citation or id relies on needs a disposition: re-point, retire the id, or record the evidence as moved.
3. **Modified-not-added seams.** Rank the window's most-churned *existing* files and subsystems, and check each against its carried id. A large delta on a carried id must not be filed "unchanged".
4. **Cross-repo FLOWs, consumer side included.** Inventory the simple-dispatcher change set, not only its LIN-id overlaps with Harbour. For every Harbour-scored FLOW that crosses into the consumer, cite consumer-side evidence for its delta, or say why there is none.
5. **Area registry cross-check (new this run).** Both repos now have an area registry (`docs/areas/areas.json`) with one note per area. Map every surface id to its area(s). An area that holds production code but maps to no surface is a coverage gap to explain. A lot of production code falling through to LinearViewer's `^lib/` catch-all (Other features) is itself worth recording.

## 3. Orientation (seeds only, as of 2026-11-10; discover the real set yourself)

**Window size.**

* **LinearViewer:** `git rev-list --count c5694b68..origin/main` = **450** commits. Measured from `38760071`, it is 448 commits, 255 of them touching `lib/`, `routes/` or `server.js`.
  * **Added:** 98 files under `lib`+`routes` (61 `lib/`, 14 `lib/components/`, 4 `lib/prompts/`, 1 `lib/sample-data/`, 18 `routes/`), plus 8 under `public/`.
  * **Deleted:** 5 files: `lib/next-run.js`, `lib/render-next-run.js`, `routes/next-run.js`, `lib/task-cost.js` and `lib/plan-fee-config.js`.
* **simple-dispatcher:** `bb1da78..origin/main` = **67** commits, 255 files, +47,108/−3,427. Most of that is the test harness: 123 added files under `test/`. The new root modules are `env-flag.js`, `instance-guard.js`, `state-dir.js`, `request-usage.js`, `request-usage-flush.js` and `opencode-request-records.js`.

Re-measure all of these numbers yourself.

**Largest modified seam: the session-auth workspace API was split.** `routes/workspace-api.js` is now 916 lines, beside nine `routes/workspace-api-*.js` siblings: `-issue-write`, `-issue-read`, `-run-evidence`, `-feedback`, `-roadmap`, `-prompts`, `-scan`, `-steps` and `-audit`. Every run-4 citation into `workspace-api.js` (R7's `:3410` / `:3455` / `:3655` / `:815`, R1, the recommendation-input importers) must be re-pointed by content. At mint time, `defaultMarkDone` / `settleDone` live in `routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js`. `checkPeriodicalReportGate` is still imported only by `routes/proxy-writes.js` (`refusedByPeriodicalGate`), and LIN-2576 is still **Todo**. So R7 may be in its **fifth** cycle. Verify that every Done writer is still ungated before you say so.

**The periodical lane itself was rebuilt.** This touches `flow-periodicals-two-stage` (R1, R7, R9) and this review's own META surface:

* **LIN-4349 / 4379 / 4380:** corrective periodicals now feed the area notes and mint nothing.
* **LIN-4381:** the "landed" due-state. Check whether this supersedes LIN-1629 (Todo).
* **LIN-4313 / 4317:** mint by registry id through the proxy.
* **LIN-4390:** the run hands off, and close-out merges and sets Done.
* **LIN-4353 / 4362:** the As-asked seal (`lib/as-asked*.js`).
* **LIN-4389 (Todo):** advisory periodicals still describe minting that no longer happens. This is direct META evidence about this template.

Confirm in `lib/periodicals.js` that advisory templates render without `notes`. That is why this run writes no area-note entries.

**Candidate new or changed surfaces visible at mint** (classify them; don't assume these are right):

* **Area notes / leftover flow (cross-repo FLOW candidate).** LinearViewer: `docs/areas/`, `lib/dispatch-leftover{,-hook}.js`, `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` (`LEFTOVER_RULE`), `lib/prompts/area-registry-path.js`. simple-dispatcher: `docs/areas/` (LIN-4372). Tickets: LIN-4347, LIN-4371, LIN-4374, LIN-4376.
* **Per-request usage records (cross-repo FLOW candidate).** simple-dispatcher: `request-usage{,-flush}.js`, `opencode-request-records.js` (LIN-4195/4197/4199/4202/4203; the OpenCode posting is "behind an unwired seam", so check run 4's R8 shape). LinearViewer: `lib/request-usage-{intake,store,fold,loader,vocabulary}.js`, `lib/usage-snapshot-intake.js`, `lib/row-usage.js`, `lib/cost-{read,format}.js`, replacing the deleted `lib/task-cost.js`.
* **Model routing:** `lib/model-routing*.js` (8 files), `routes/proxy-model-routing.js`, `routes/settings-model.js`.
* **Runner kit contract (carried** `api-runner-kit`**, R14).** simple-dispatcher LIN-4385 ("the contract test knows its areas, and checks each column against sd") and LIN-4378 (the broker's 429 policy pinned against the runner contract). Decide whether R14, "the contract pin is guarded by no CI", has moved, and on which side.
* **As-asked / size of move / stage writes:** `lib/as-asked{,-seal}.js`, `lib/size-of-move.js`, `lib/stage-writes.js`, `lib/recommendation-look-first.js`.
* **Dashboard / home / settings UI lanes:** `routes/dashboard-*.js` (7 files), `lib/home-*.js`, `routes/settings.js`, `lib/settings-*.js`, `lib/render-settings-*.js`, `lib/components/settings-*.js`, `routes/getting-started.js`.
* **Next-run retirement:** 3 of the 5 deleted files. Check whether any run-4 id depends on them.
* **Others:** `lib/connection-secondary-remint.js` (R13's lane), `lib/key-state*.js`, `lib/ruling-{settled,standing}.js`, `lib/call-budget.js`, `lib/catalog-rate.js`, `lib/close-out-merges.js`, `lib/workspace-change-log.js`, `lib/vendor-assets.js`, and simple-dispatcher's `instance-guard.js` / `state-dir.js` / `env-flag.js`.

**Consumer-repository decision.** Run 4's ledger unit is the Harbour-served surface, so consumer internals are unscored by design. Its second-read accepted that the consumer change set went un-inventoried. Re-take the decision explicitly at HEAD (LIN-1933, target-repo selection, is still **Todo**). Whatever you decide, sweep pass 4 above is not optional.

## 4. Carried recommendations: where each appears to stand (verify, don't trust)

| id | run-4 status | mint-time pointer (re-confirm at HEAD) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| R7 | open, #1, 4th cycle | Gate only in `routes/proxy-writes.js`; Done writers moved by the workspace-api split. LIN-2576 **Todo**. |
| R13 | open | LIN-2150 **Todo**; new `lib/connection-secondary-remint.js`. Owned by Security Review. |
| R1 | open, improved | LIN-3649 **Backlog**; periodical lane rebuilt (§3). |
| R14 | open, new | See the runner-kit bullet in §3. |
| R2 | open, partly improved | LIN-2120 **Backlog**. |
| R9 | open | LIN-2846 **Backlog**. |
| R16 | META, new | Re-count how many done/High surfaces real findings hit this window. |
| R15 | open | Heartbeat auth-stop field stored but not shown. Owner: Observability (LIN-1041). |
| R3 | open | LIN-1040 Reliability and LIN-1041 Observability are both **Backlog**. Neither is among the 16 registry templates. |
| R12 | worsened 5→19 | Documentation Review owns it. Its latest report is still 2026-10-21; a run was dispatched 2026-11-10 and may land during this run. |
| R8, R6, R11, R17 | open | R6 likely improved: Performance/Scale and Data & Fetch Architecture each produced a first report on 2026-10-23. |
| R4, R5, R10 | resolved | Stay closed unless regressed. LIN-3074 was still Backlog at mint, though R10 was resolved in code. |

Unresolved recommendations carry forward under their original ids. New ones start at **R18**.

## 5. Sibling evidence: freshness and owners (re-list `docs/reviews/` immediately before scoring)

`GET /api/proxy/periodicals` reports dispatch recency, not report freshness. Read the files themselves. Since LIN-4380, corrective siblings record findings in `docs/areas/*.md` **Waiting/Lessons entries** ("(<Periodical title>, <date>)") as well as in their reports, so read both.

At mint time, the newest edition of each sibling was:

* **2026-10-23 wave:** API Quality, Test Coverage Gap, Security, Dependency & Supply-Chain, Onboarding & Cold-Start, and the **first** Performance/Scale and Data & Fetch Architecture reports.
* **Fresher:** Code Quality (11-04), Comprehension-Debt (11-05), Design & Interface (11-08), Stability (11-04, 11-08), Seams & Tangles (through `-2026-11-10-run11`), Drift & Coherence (through 11-10).
* **Oldest:** Documentation and Recent Headwinds (10-21).

Judge each one current or stale for the dimensions you score from it. A report existing is not the same as a report being current.

**Owner map (name the owner; don't re-home the fix):**

* Error handling, resilience, rate limits & pagination, and idempotency & consistency belong to **Reliability** (LIN-1040, not built).
* Observability belongs to **Observability** (LIN-1041, not built).
* Auth & credentials and security belong to **Security Review**.
* Input & schema validation belongs to **API Quality Review**.
* Testing belongs to **Test Coverage Gap Review**.
* Documentation belongs to **Documentation Review**.

Name Reliability and Observability even though neither exists. Don't absorb their remit, and don't block on them. If a newer sibling (Performance/Scale, Data & Fetch Architecture, Seams & Tangles) now plausibly owns or evidences a dimension, cite its remit and record that as a META delta.

## 6. Run the review

**Inventory.** Classify every part of the system that can be more or less "done" into exactly one of four types:

* **MOD:** a structural module or component.
* **API:** an integration or boundary that crosses a trust or process boundary, such as an external dependency or an internal service call.
* **FLOW:** a concept or entity that traverses multiple modules, is owned by no single one, and may be only partly wired end-to-end. Give these **extra scrutiny**, because they are the ones most often left half-finished.
* **META:** this review's own methodology.

Reuse every run-4 id **verbatim**. An id is forever: a removed surface is marked **retired**, never deleted. New ids get stable, descriptive names.

**Score** every surface on the twelve dimensions, each 0 (absent) to 4 (hardened), or N/A when it genuinely doesn't apply:

 1. core/happy path
 2. error handling & failure modes
 3. resilience (timeouts, retries with backoff, circuit breaking, graceful degradation)
 4. rate limits & pagination
 5. auth & credentials (refresh, rotation, expiry, least privilege)
 6. idempotency & consistency
 7. input & schema validation
 8. observability
 9. security
10. testing (including contract tests for API surfaces)
11. documentation
12. configuration (env-specific config, feature flags, safe defaults)

Cite concrete evidence (a path, a symbol, or a specific sibling report and finding) for **any score of 0–1 or 4**, and for **every score that changed since run 4**. These dimensions and finding classes are **examples, not a limit**. Discover the complete set for this remit from the repo. A class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.

**Prefer existing evidence. Use bounded first-party inspection only to fill gaps.** For each dimension, first look for current, sufficient evidence in sibling reports, area notes, project docs and related tickets. Where it is fresh and thorough, score from it rather than re-deriving it. Treat stale or shallow evidence as missing. Where evidence is missing, stale or shallow, do a *bounded* first-party look at the code to fill that specific gap.

Mark every surface's confidence **High / Medium / Low**. A Low from a quick look is honest; a High with no current source is not. A bounded first-party pass never implies this review now owns a sibling's remit.

**Mind the altitude.** For a sibling-owned dimension, summarise maturity and coverage only. Never re-derive the sibling's findings, and never mint or re-home a fix into its territory. Name the owning review as the home for deeper follow-up. This review's own first-party remit is FLOW surfaces, core/happy path, configuration and the portfolio/META scorecard. Everything else is aggregation.

**Measurement discipline.**

* The per-surface, per-dimension ledger with cited evidence is the primary signal.
* Portfolio **Completeness %** is secondary and explicitly noisy. Never cite a Completeness % delta without naming which surfaces moved and why, and spell out the denominator effect of new surfaces.
* Persist **every N/A with its justification** in the state section. A dimension flipping to or from N/A is a reportable delta, never a silent denominator change. One more N/A must not read as improvement.
* A changed score with no cited evidence is scorer drift: record it as **unchanged**.

**Rank the findings.** Emit each recommendation as an object with these fields:

* `id`
* `surface`
* `dimension`
* `finding` (with cited evidence)
* `action`
* `impact` (H/M/L)
* `effort` (H/M/L)
* `priority` (derived: highest impact and lowest effort first)
* `status`
* `owner` (this review, or the named sibling)

Cap the headline list a human is asked to read at the **top 5–10 by priority**. The full set stays in the machine-readable state section. An unresolved recommendation carries forward under its original id.

**Self-audit (META surface** `meta-integration-surface-maturity-review`**).** Score this review's own methodology and answer each of these:

* How many surfaces are stuck at Low confidence, and why?
* Did a real finding elsewhere land on a surface this review had rated done? That is a scoring-model gap; run 4 counted 14 of 35 (R16). Seed: the LIN-3642 OAuth fix (Done) on `flow-oauth`, and area-note Waiting entries citing files under High-rated surfaces.
* Is any dimension consistently N/A (dead weight) or consistently 0 (possibly unmeasurable here)?
* Are past top recommendations being acted on? R7 may be at five cycles. R3 has been unchanged since the baseline.
* Did the five-pass sweep catch what run 4 missed (the consumer change set, `public/`)?
* Does this template's own text still describe behaviour that changed (LIN-4389)?

Turn what you find into recommendations against the META surface, like any other surface.

## 7. Write the report

Write an **uncapped, severity-ranked, trend-framed** report. Finding nothing, one thing or many things are all valid outcomes. Do not pad, cap or invent make-work. Ground every finding at HEAD or in the sibling evidence you cite, never in prior prose. Re-point every run-4 citation into a changed or deleted file, and verify each one by content.

Include these sections:

* re-grounding (fetch, HEAD pins, drift)
* scope & sweep accounting (all five passes)
* consumer-repo decision
* headline read
* findings
* surface registration (new, folded, retired)
* the twelve-dimension scorecard with owner and confidence
* sibling-owned coverage
* Self-Audit
* Completeness %
* a plain-language read for the maintainer

Close with a compact **Trend Ledger**. For every id, give the type, the scores, severity, the delta vs run 4, Completeness and confidence, area(s), and any N/A with its justification, so the next run can diff it mechanically.

## 8. Report back for a human decision: mint NO follow-up tasks

This review is a portfolio governor. **Do not create follow-up tasks or sub-issues, and do not write area-note entries.** Do not mint or re-home a fix into a sibling's territory. Even a high-severity finding on a sibling-owned dimension goes to the human as a pointer to its owning review or existing ticket. End the report with the ranked recommendations, the scorecard and the self-audit findings, and leave triage to the human.

## 9. Stay review-only

Producing the report changes no code, config or secrets, and no docs beyond the report artifact and its evidence folder. An instruction to avoid touching files is about the code and docs *under review*. It does not override this task's own deliverable.

## 10. Adversarial second-read (required, structural, before hand-off)

After the report is written and before the hand-off, a genuinely separate reader must answer one question cold: *"What is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

* **Tier 1 (preferred):** a wholly separate session with no memory of this run.
* **Tier 2 (accepted fallback):** a fresh-context sub-agent with no memory of the report-writing turn. Give it the report path, both repo roots, both windows and the remit, but not your findings.
* **Tier 3 (this session re-reading its own report) is not accepted.**

Post **one** comment on this task that contains all three of these lines together:

* `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
* `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO`. This records whether the reader's answer differs from the report's own top-ranked finding, independent of the verdict.
* `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`

The engine refuses Done until all three are present in one comment body. Copy the same fields into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report, with the tier used, the question and the reader's full answer. AGREE and DISAGREE both proceed to the normal hand-off; a DISAGREE is itself the escalation.

## 11. Hand off (do not merge or set Done yourself)

1. As soon as the report PR is open, post its **full URL** as a comment on this task. The engine requires it before Done.
2. Leave the PR rebased onto `main` and green (`ci-success`).
3. After the second-read comment, post a closing comment with these parts:
   * a concise, severity-ranked summary of the report: the top recommendations with their deltas, a scorecard headline and the self-audit findings
   * a path or link to the full report
   * who finishes: review approves, then close-out merges the report PR, sets this task to Done and posts the final summary

This run neither merges nor moves the task to Done, and the task stays In Progress until close-out finishes. If the PR cannot be made green, name the blocker in the closing comment instead. Escalating never blocks the hand-off.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the fifth trend-framed maturity report as asked; no Survey finding binds, since the report works without fixing the ungated Done paths or the template drift, which it records as findings for the human.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out, 2026-11-10. The research findings and the full plan (its decisions, witnesses and order of work) are kept in the task snapshots (archived 2026-11-10T12:32:44Z) and the comment trail.*

**What was implemented.** The fifth Integration & Surface Maturity report and its evidence folder, `docs/reviews/integration-surface-maturity-review-2026-11-10.md` and `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-10-ism/`. They landed through PR [#2389](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2389>), squash-merged as `730df21c2` and deployed. The plan was implemented as approved. The one deviation is the review's close-out condition: a prose-only item (7) in the report's Adversarial Second-Read paragraph (commit `378a8cee4`). It records that `flow-dispatch-lifecycle` and `flow-dispatch-halt` CFG stay carried N/A\* and are open for run 6's configuration pass.

**Size:** fits one session. It is long, but the bookkeeping that would otherwise be lost lives in committed files, not the session's memory: the sweep sums, the citation table and the JSON ledger. The second-read runs as a sub-agent, and nothing touches code. The block also forbids sub-issues, so the work could not be split into child tickets anyway.

plan-review due: no. It is docs-only. It loosens no guard, routes around no cause, and touches no credentials, merge rules or the dispatch contract. The deliverable already gets two independent readers (the §10 second-read and the review stage).

## Survey open-0: LIN-4407 @ ecabd3d76

Read at LinearViewer `ecabd3d76`; simple-dispatcher is still `5d8489e`.

**The mint numbers are already out of date.** LIN-4404 (task-life cost read) landed after `f5b1f5efa` and touches `lib/cost-read.js` and `docs/areas/areas.json`. Since `c5694b68` the window is **454** commits, with **107** files added under lib/routes/public and **10** deleted, not 5. The extra five are `public/{chart.umd.min,marked.min,purify.min,next-run}.js` and `public/next-run.css`, which suggests the vendored libraries moved behind `lib/vendor-assets.js`.

**Why it's hard**

1. **The report is mostly bookkeeping.** It has 51+ ids × 12 dimensions, five sweep passes that have to balance exactly, and every citation into the old `workspace-api.js` re-pointed by content across ten files (5,213 lines combined). The second-reads on runs 3 and 4 both caught filing errors. It will go wrong in the ledger, not in the judgement.
2. **R7 has spread.** `checkPeriodicalReportGate` is imported only by `routes/proxy-writes.js:54`. `settleDone`/`defaultMarkDone` (`routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js:47,224`) write Done without it. So does the session issue edit (`routes/workspace-api-issue-write.js:832-861`, which sets `stateId` and never calls the gate). That's at least two ungated Done writers, so it's a fifth cycle. The hard part is saying something better than "still open". If LIN-4390's close-out Done goes through the gated proxy, then the gate covers the *intended* path while the session routes stay open. That's the sharper framing.
3. **The template partly misdescribes itself (META).** `lib/periodicals.js:114` says advisory templates mint nothing. But `adversarialRead({notes:false})` still renders "(and any follow-up tasks)" (`:382`). That's LIN-4389 in code. And the scoring model whose done/High ratings missed 14 of 35 real findings (R16) hasn't changed.
4. **The area catch-all is where new work lands.** All 18 `lib/` files that fall through to `^lib/` (Other features) were added in this window: `home-*`, `key-state*`, `ruling-*`, `stage-writes`, `as-asked-seal`, `usage-snapshot-intake`, `cost-format`, `task-state`, and others. They're the candidate new surfaces.
5. **The consumer side is heavy in tests and light in surfaces.** It has +47k lines, mostly `test/`. Per-request usage does cross over: `opencode-runner.js:91` now requires `opencode-request-records`. So the "unwired seam" claim, and whether R8 has moved, has to be checked on the consumer side.

**What I'd do first**

Before scoring, generate two tables by script and commit them as evidence:
(a) every run-4 citation → its HEAD location, found by content;
(b) every added, deleted and most-churned file → area slug → surface id or exclusion.
Those two tables are what tripped up the last two second-reads. Pick a fresh evidence folder name: `_evidence-2026-11-10-drift` and `-run11` already exist.

Then settle R7 by listing every code path that can write a `completed` state and counting them against the gate. Don't rely on the ticket status.

**Is the ticket aimed at a symptom?** Partly. A fifth cycle on R7, and R3 unchanged since the baseline, show the series reports well but nothing turns its top recommendation into owned work.
